pull.title: KAFKA-21278: interactive-queries.md still states the removed methods
pull.body:
The Interactive Queries guide still used APIs that were removed a long
time ago, including `metadataForKey`, `allMetadata`, and
`allMetadataForStore`. Update the guide and its examples to use the
current metadata APIs. Also fix a few nearby outdated code snippets and
links while touching the same document. Verified the documentation links
with `./gradlew :streams:javadoc`.

Reviewers: liuliu <liuliugit@gmail.com>, Matthias J. Sax
 <matthias@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:
Thanks. Made a pass.

Few more things we could address, but it's not a must:
```
  (1) The Headers overloads of queryMetadataForKey are missing from the list. They were added in 4.4 by KIP-1321 (cba250ead1). Their Javadoc warns that without them, a partitioner or serializer that reads headers can return the wrong host. This
  page already covers headers at length, and the PR's goal is to document the current API, so one more sentence would fit.

  (2) The new "Attention" sentence could be more exact. "queryMetadataForKey() cannot provide a usable host" is accurate, but you can say what actually happens. StreamsMetadataState only builds metadata for hosts that set application.server, so
  the active-host lookup never finds the owning instance. activeHost() then returns HostInfo.unavailable() ("unavailable", port -1), and a standby on that instance is simply absent from standbyHosts(). Saying so tells the reader what to check
  for.

  (3) The two queryMetadataForKey bullets still say "find the one application instance that holds the data". The new lead-in sentence says the method returns the active and standby instances, so the bullets now contradict it. Something like "find
  the active and standby instances for the key" would match.
```

 A wrapper class is required because each instance of a Kafka Streams application may run multiple stream tasks and manage multiple local instances of a particular state store. The wrapper class hides this complexity and lets you query a "logical" state store by name without having to know about all of the underlying local instances of that state store.
 
-When implementing your wrapper class you must use the [StateStoreProvider](https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/4.4/streams/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/streams/state/internals/StateStoreProvider.java) interface to get access to the underlying instances of your store. `StateStoreProvider#stores(String storeName, QueryableStoreType<T> queryableStoreType)` returns a `List` of state stores with the given storeName and of the type as defined by `queryableStoreType`.
+When implementing your wrapper class you must use the [StateStoreProvider](https://github.com/apache/kafka/blob/trunk/streams/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/streams/state/internals/StateStoreProvider.java) interface to get access to the underlying instances of your store. `StateStoreProvider#stores(String storeName, QueryableStoreType<T> queryableStoreType)` returns a `List` of state stores with the given storeName and of the type as defined by `queryableStoreType`.

 ## Discovering and accessing application instances and their local state stores
 
-The following methods return [StreamsMetadata](/{version}/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/streams/state/StreamsMetadata.html) objects, which provide meta-information about application instances such as their RPC endpoint and locally available state stores.
+The following methods return [StreamsMetadata](/{version}/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/streams/StreamsMetadata.html) objects, which provide meta-information about application instances such as their RPC endpoint and locally available state stores.
 
-  * `KafkaStreams#allMetadata()`: find all instances of this application
-  * `KafkaStreams#allMetadataForStore(String storeName)`: find those applications instances that manage local instances of the state store "storeName"
-  * `KafkaStreams#metadataForKey(String storeName, K key, Serializer<K> keySerializer)`: using the default stream partitioning strategy, find the one application instance that holds the data for the given key in the given state store
-  * `KafkaStreams#metadataForKey(String storeName, K key, StreamPartitioner<K, ?> partitioner)`: using `partitioner`, find the one application instance that holds the data for the given key in the given state store
+  * `KafkaStreams#metadataForAllStreamsClients()`: find all instances of this application
+  * `KafkaStreams#streamsMetadataForStore(String storeName)`: find those applications instances that manage local instances of the state store "storeName"
